This brief presents a novel time-domain bitmap compression implementation, converts activation compression into activation serialization and pulse compression, eliminating the need for area and power consuming crossbar network or inverse butterfly network commonly used in parallel approaches. First, it utilizes pulses generated by a cascaded buffer delay chain to convert parallel activation into a serialized stream. Then, a pulse compression circuit is introduced to squeeze pulses corresponding to invalid activation and generate time-alignment sampling clock for the serialized stream. Finally, compressed activation is stored in proposed single-phase rising-clocked registers which explore the characteristics of activation and clock to reduce power consumption. Simulated in 28nm CMOS technology, the proposed method achieves a 68% reduction in circuit area for 128 8-bit activation compression compared to existing parallel approaches, and reduces energy per operation by 31.3%, 43.5%, 46.6%, and 24.3% for activation lengths of 16, 32, 64, and 128, respectively.

item.title: LLC Resonant Converter-Based Embedded EIS Measurement Method for Lithium-Ion Battery
item.description: An embedded electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurement method is proposed for lithium-ion batteries based on an LLC resonant converter. By superimposing a small-signal sinusoidal perturbation onto the constant-current reference and exploiting the frequency-dependent gain characteristics of the LLC resonant converter under pulse-frequency modulation (PFM), the battery impedance is extracted through synchronous voltage and current sampling. To ensure stable perturbation injection and measurement accuracy, the small-signal behavior of the LLC resonant converter under battery load is analyzed, where the lithium battery is modeled as a second-order RC equivalent model. The influence of load-impedance magnitude and phase on the converter gain characteristics is clarified, and the effective operating range for EIS excitation is identified. A PI-regulated current loop is also designed to confine the switching frequency within the resonant region, achieving non-destructive measurement without additional analog front-end hardware. Experimental results shows that the proposed method can achieve accurate EIS measurement from 0.1Hz to 2kHz with a low normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE) of 2.24% under different states of charge (SOCs).

item.title: FPGA Deployment of Extremely Quantized Models for Time-to-Lane-Change Prediction
item.description: Despite the rapid evolution of automated driving, public information about deployability in production vehicles remains limited. We present a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) prototyping study of an AI module for estimating time-to-lane-change (TTLC), focusing on key deployment metrics such as latency, memory footprint, and power/energy consumption. FPGAs enable custom acceleration while providing flexibility to explore multiple design trade-offs. Particularly, we investigate different quantization strategies, given their potential to substantially reduce model size while preserving predictive performance. This brief makes four main contributions that advance the state-of-the-art through an FPGA-based implementation. We present a hardware-aware FPGA design methodology that balances memory efficiency and task accuracy. We provide a comprehensive analysis of the trade-offs achievable by varying AI model type, operating frequency, and quantization precision. We find a set of Pareto-optimal solutions along the power-latency axes, identifying a clear elbow at a co-processor frequency of 25/50 MHz depending on model and quantization type. We implement a Transformer architecture that preserves state-of-the-art TTLC predictive performance while meeting the 10 Hz real-time constraint and reducing total energy consumption by 83% compared to a high-end microcontroller.

item.title: EDACurry: A Multilanguage Framework to Create, Translate, and Manipulate Transistor-Level Netlists
item.description: The simulation program with integrated circuit emphasis (SPICE), introduced in 1973, laid the foundation for transistor-level netlist representation. Over the decades, numerous SPICE dialects emerged, each tailored to specific needs but sharing core semantics. This article presents EDACurry, an innovative, open-source framework designed to simplify and automate the creation, translation, and manipulation of transistor-level netlists across SPICE-based languages such as Eldo and Spectre. By leveraging a unified internal abstract syntax tree (AST), EDACurry bridges syntactical differences while maintaining semantic consistency, enabling efficient manipulation workflows. The framework supports custom operations, including design space exploration, defect model injection, and subcircuit wrapping, all accessible through Python. Demonstrated applications highlight its versatility in analog design workflows, offering integration with commercial and open-source simulators. With EDACurry, analog designers gain a powerful tool to support netlist manipulation tasks, improving productivity and fostering innovation in circuit design. The entire framework is publicly available on GitHub: https://github.com/esd-univr/EDACurry

item.title: Design and Evaluation of an RFET Standard Cell Library Compatible With 22-nm FDSOI
item.description: Reconfigurable field-effect transistor (RFET) is an emerging technology that offers runtime reconfigurability between n-type and p-type operation modes. Its unique features, including intrinsic polymorphism, symmetric $I-V$ characteristics, multiple independent gate control, and low leakage current, unlock new possibilities for designing energy-efficient logic circuits, particularly polymorphic ones well-suited for hardware security techniques such as logic locking. Although various RFET device realizations with different materials and structures have been proposed, only a few studies have developed standard cell libraries that enable the evaluation of large-scale circuits implemented with these technologies. Moreover, the existing libraries are not designed according to the design rules of well-established industrial processes. This article presents standard cell libraries comprising both static and reconfigurable logic cells, enabling a complete RTL-to-GDSII flow for three-independent-gate RFETs (TIG-RFETs), compatible with an industrial 22-nm FDSOI technology. We implement the circuits from the ISCAS’85 and EPFL’15 benchmark suites using our libraries within a commercial electronic design automation (EDA) tool flow and compare the synthesis results with their CMOS counterparts in the same technology node in terms of power, performance, and area (PPA). The results demonstrate that TIG-RFETs can significantly reduce power consumption, though with a performance tradeoff that limits the achievable clock frequency to a few megahertz. Furthermore, we analyze the results to highlight the advantages and limitations of this implementation of TIG-RFETs and discuss potential future improvements.

item.title: Rail Routing for Power Distribution Networks in Advanced Multilayered Printed Circuit Boards
item.description: Power distribution networks (PDNs) are designed to deliver sufficient and stable power to printed circuit board (PCB) components. With increasing current/voltage demands on modern PCBs, power rails in PDN require more space for metals. Existing design techniques often adopt greedy heuristics to optimize the metal shapes of power rails. However, they consider little spatial competition among different power rails, so routing spaces may be distributed unevenly, causing redundant metal usage, current/voltage violations, and even routing failures in high-current designs. To remedy this problem, we propose a multilayered PDN design flow to distribute rail spaces according to current/voltage demands appropriately. To our knowledge, this is the first work to consider the spatial competition issue in PCB power rail routing. Specifically, we generate a multilayered topology and minimize the metal area and the via usage with mathematical programming. To resolve the overlap regions by rail detouring, we also propose a resistance-aware routing algorithm. Experimental results show that our work significantly outperforms a baseline algorithm extended from the state-of-the-art rail router in the metal area and runtime, achieving respective reductions of 55% and 71%, without any current/voltage violations.

item.title: GAP-LA: GPU-Accelerated Performance-Driven Layer Assignment
item.description: Layer assignment is critical for global routing of VLSI circuits. It converts 2-D routing paths into 3-D routing solutions by determining the proper metal layer for each routing segments to minimize congestion and via count. As different layers have different unit resistance and capacitance, layer assignment also has significant impacts to timing and power. With growing design complexity, it becomes increasingly challenging to simultaneously optimize timing, power, and congestion efficiently. Existing studies are mostly limited to a subset of objectives. In this article, we propose a GPU-accelerated performance-driven layer assignment GAP-LA framework, for holistic optimization the aforementioned objectives. Experimental results demonstrate that we can achieve 0.3%–9.9% better worst negative slack (WNS) and 2.0%–5.4% better total negative slack (TNS) while maintaining power and congestion with competitive runtime compared with ISPD 2025 contest winners, especially on designs with up to 12 millions of nets. We also apply our method to the 2-D net topology of ISPD 2025 contest winners. Compared with their original flow, we achieve 8.5%–18.3% better WNS and 2.0%–5.1% better TNS.

item.title: Easyn: Resynthesis and Legalization Joint NIMCH Design Placement
item.description: Noninteger multiple cell height (NIMCH) libraries have been adopted by advanced manufacturers in the latest technology node to offer better power efficiency, performance optimization, and area occupancy. However, in order to meet manufacturing requirements, such as power supply, NIMCH placement must comply with several additional layout restrictions. Currently, the state-of-the-art method applies resynthesis and legalization to the initial placement result to achieve a minimum displacement. However, the two decoupled phases lead to a reduction in the solution space and an insensitivity to timing. Therefore, we propose an iterative algorithm with a corresponding data structure, which comprehensively considers displacement and timing information. Experiments demonstrate that our method can generate legalized NIMCH designs with a lower maximum delay and a reduced area.

item.title: 2-D Analytical Surface Potential Modeling and Simulation-Based Optimization of GoP-HD-DMDG-TFET for Enhanced Performance
item.description: This work presents a comprehensive surface potential analysis of the gate-over-pockets heterodielectric dual-metal double-gate tunnel field-effect transistor (GoP-HD-DMDG-TFET). The impact of pockets, dielectric thickness and permittivity, gate material work function, silicon body thickness, and gate and drain voltages are taken into account. An analytical model developed using the 2-D Poisson’s equation is validated against Sentaurus TCAD simulations. The impact of critical design parameters on the performance of GoP-HD-DMDG-TFET is investigated. The influence of pocket length ( $L_{\text {poc}}$ ), tunneling-to-auxiliary gate length ratio ( $L_{\text {tunn}}:L_{\text {aux}}$ ), pocket thickness ( $t_{\text {poc}}$ ), and work function variation is systematically analyzed to optimize device performance for improved subthreshold behavior, on-current, and $I_{\text {ON}}/I_{\text {OFF}}$ ratio. Results indicate that a larger $L_{\text {poc}}$ indicates a trade-off between improved on-state performance and increased leakage current, with reduced subthreshold swing (SS). Moreover, tuning the tunneling-to-auxiliary gate length ratio ( $L_{\text {tunn}}:L_{\text {aux}}$ ) significantly affects electrostatic control, influencing threshold voltage ( $V_{\text {th}}$ ) and on-current ( $I_{\text {ON}}$ ). In addition, the pocket thickness ( $t_{\text {poc}}$ ) is optimized to 4 nm, yielding the steepest SS and highest $I_{\text {on}}/I_{\text {off}}$ ratio. Work function engineering provides an effective approach to modulate the potential barrier and optimize leakage characteristics. These insights highlight the design flexibility of GoP-HD-DMDG-TFET, making it a promising candidate for ultralow-power and high-performance circuit applications.

item.title: Machine Learning-Based Timing and Power Models for Multiple-Input Switching and Glitch Effects
item.description: With continuous technology scaling, accurate and efficient multiple-input switching (MIS) modeling is essential for designing high-performance, low-power, and reliable integrated circuits (ICs). MIS commonly induces speedup or slow-down effects on gate timing and may even generate spurious glitches at the outputs, potentially impacting timing, power consumption, and overall circuit reliability. In this article, we propose a unified MIS modeling approach based on machine learning (ML), employing efficient and compact artificial neural networks (ANNs) to estimate the timing and power characteristics of MIS-induced transitions and glitches. To achieve this, we evaluate various ML engines and explore different ANN hyperparameters and architectures. Moreover, we introduce an iterative workflow that seamlessly integrates our ANNs into standard cell libraries, striking an optimal balance between model accuracy and size. The proposed framework employs efficient techniques to reduce characterization effort, minimize library size, and improve model accuracy. Experimental evaluation on gates implemented in 7-nm FinFET and 45-nm bulk CMOS technologies indicates that our models exhibit a strong correlation with SPICE, achieving a mean $R^{2}$ score of 0.997 across all gates and process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) corners while maintaining low-memory demands. Thus, our approach can effectively improve gate-level timing, power, and reliability analysis and guide glitch reduction techniques.

item.title: An Area-Efficient SiC-MOSFET Termination Optimization Method Based on Deep Learning and Specified MOPSO Algorithm
item.description: The breakdown and reliability performance of silicon carbide (SiC) power devices is greatly affected by edge termination design. However, considering the complexity of parameters and the tradeoff between multiple objectives, it is a challenging process to achieve high breakdown voltage (BV) and area efficiency simultaneously in typical termination structures like the field-limit ring (FLR). To address the problem, this article proposes a novel and efficient termination design optimization method based on physically characterized variables. With the utilization of auxiliary parameter $\gamma $ specified multiple objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) algorithm, a 110-V improvement in BV and more than 26% reduction in termination area have been achieved, respectively. Importantly, the design scheme provided by this method demonstrates superiority over the dataset utilized during training. The results are validated by technology computer aided design (TCAD) simulation, and we also successfully predicted the performance gain of the actual manufactured devices. Therefore, this article offers a potential solution approach for multiobjective optimization problems. With the diverse distribution of Pareto solutions, this method proves broad applicability in the design of power devices involving multiobjective optimization.

item.title: A Physics-Constrained Neural Network Method for Compact Modeling of Semiconductor Devices
item.description: This work proposes a physics-constrained neural network (PCNN) method for automated and physically consistent compact modeling of semiconductor devices. Traditional artificial neural network (ANN)-based approaches often exhibit limited enforcement of physical monotonicity and symmetry, suffer from poor generalization, and require complex manual data preprocessing. The proposed method addresses these challenges through two core innovations: a self-adaptive data preprocessing strategy that eliminates manual intervention, and a weight-generation neural architecture that embeds physics-inspired constraints to ensure monotonicity and symmetry. Extensive device- and circuit-level evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of the method. On average, a $3.2\times $ reduction in mean relative error (MRE) is achieved in modeling $I$ – $V$ and $C$ – $V$ characteristics across the devices evaluated in this work compared with ANN-based models. In circuit-level simulations, the method reduces the power-delay product (PDP) error from 50% to 7% in a 17-stage ring oscillator (RO) and lowers the gain error from 5.7% to 0.4% in a common-source amplifier. In addition, transient simulation time is reduced by up to 70% compared to ANN-based models. These results highlight that the proposed method not only improves physical consistency and modeling accuracy but also enables scalable and efficient SPICE-level simulation, paving the way for practical AI-/ML-assisted compact model development.

item.title: TriM-D: Accelerating 2-D/3-D Diffusion Generation Via Triple-Mixed Quantization and Sparsity-Aware Dual-Branched Computation
item.description: Diffusion models have shown marked advancements in 2-D generation and have also become focal points in 3-D generation via consistent multiview image generation. However, the computation and memory demands hinder their real-time deployment on mobile and edge devices. Moreover, the reduction of diffusion timesteps leads to a decrease in interstep similarity, thereby making previous methods ineffective in optimizing computation. The varied layer quantization sensitivity and optimal format in diffusion models also present challenges for traditional quantization methods to achieve efficient memory compression. To address these issues, we first introduce ${M}^{3}$ quantization, a mixed-precision, mixed-format, and mixed-granularity quantization framework that allocates optimal precision and format to different data with a unified FP8 computation flow for efficient implementation. Building upon ${M}^{3}$ quantization, we present TriM-D, a hardware accelerator designed to optimize computation. It features sparsity-aware dual-branched FP8-MAC units that introduce a dual-branch path and an efficient approximate adder to fully utilize bit-level sparsity of ${M}^{3}$ -quantized data. Such an FP8-MAC scheme preserves both efficiency and numerical accuracy. Our experiments demonstrate that TriM-D significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art (SOTA) diffusion accelerator Cambricon-D (Camb-D), achieving an average reduction of 56.5% in memory access and 80.6% in computation cost. In addition, TriM-D provides a $55\times $ , $6.72\times $ improvement in energy efficiency and $3.69\times $ , $2.67\times $ speedups over NVIDIA A100 and Camb-D.

item.title: Optimizing Power Distribution Network in Multichiplet System With Reinforcement Learning: A Comprehensive Study on Methodology, Algorithm, and Reward Strategies
item.description: This study proposes a reinforcement learning (RL) framework to automate power distribution network (PDN) design in a redistribution layer (RDL) interposer, such as high-density fan-out wafer-level packaging (HD-FOWLP) and CoWoS-R, for multichiplet systems. A four-chiplet system with a ring topology and 28 distinct power domains is used as the target architecture. The PDN design problem is formulated as a discrete cell assignment task within a $13\times 13$ grid that represents one quadrant of the PDN. Design rules are encoded into analytical reward functions of squareness and distance to power bumps, enabling fast and physically meaningful feedback without requiring full EDA simulation during training. Two RL algorithms, dueling double deep Q-network (DDDQN) and proximal policy optimization (PPO), are evaluated. While PPO converges faster, DDDQN can deliver higher design quality due to its suitability for discrete, deterministic tasks. Further comparisons explore the impact of dense versus sparse rewards and full-quadrant as compared to quadrant-wise design scopes. Experimental results show that the proposed approach yields lower impedance than human-designed layouts and shortens design time from months to minutes. This work aims to provide a practical methodology for applying RL to complex design problems in advanced packaging, validating the usefulness of problem abstraction and reward engineering for effective PDN layout automation.

item.title: KirchhoffNet: End-to-End Analog Circuit Acceleration for ODE-Based Neural Networks
item.description: This article introduces KirchhoffNet, a novel class of neural network models inspired by the principles of analog electronic circuitry, specifically Kirchhoff’s laws. KirchhoffNet operates as an analog circuit, where the network input is represented by initial node voltages, and the output corresponds to the node voltages at a specific time. The dynamics of the node voltages are governed by learnable parameters on the edges, and the evolution of these voltages follows a system of ordinary differential equations (ODEs). Despite the absence of traditional neural network components such as convolutional layers, KirchhoffNet achieves outstanding performance across a wide range of machine-learning tasks. We further demonstrate that KirchhoffNet is capable of computing diffusion models, making it a promising candidate for accelerating modern generative AI applications. Most notably, KirchhoffNet can be implemented as a high-speed & low-power analog integrated circuit, which introduces a compelling advantage: irrespective of the number of parameters in the network, its on-chip forward calculation can always be completed within a short time. This property makes KirchhoffNet a highly attractive and scalable paradigm for implementing large-scale neural networks, opening new avenues in the realm of analog neural networks for artificial intelligence (AI).

item.title: FETTA: Flexible and Efficient Hardware Accelerator for Tensorized Neural Network Training
item.description: The increasing demand for on-device training of deep neural networks (DNNs) aims to leverage personal data for high-performance applications while addressing privacy concerns and reducing communication latency. However, resource-constrained platforms face significant challenges due to the intensive computational and memory demands of DNN training. Tensor decomposition emerges as a promising approach to compress model size without sacrificing accuracy. Nevertheless, training tensorized neural networks (TNNs) incurs nontrivial overhead and severe performance degradation on conventional accelerators due to complex tensor shaping requirements. To address these challenges, we propose FETTA, an algorithm and hardware co-optimization framework for efficient TNN training. On the algorithm side, we develop a contraction sequence search engine (CSSE) to identify the optimal contraction sequence with the minimal computational overhead. On the hardware side, FETTA features a flexible and efficient architecture equipped with a reconfigurable contraction engine (CE) array to support diverse dataflows. Furthermore, butterfly-based distribution and reduction networks are implemented to perform flexible tensor shaping operations during computation. Evaluation results demonstrate that FETTA achieves reductions of $20.5\times $ / $100.9\times $ , $567.5\times $ / $45.03\times $ , and $11609.7\times $ / $4544.8\times $ in terms of processing latency, energy, and energy-delay product (EDP) over GPU and TPU, respectively. Moreover, working on the tensorized training, FETTA outperforms prior accelerators with a speedup of $3.87\sim 14.63\times $ and an energy efficiency improvement of $1.41 \sim 2.73\times $ on average.

item.title: Quantum Multiview Feature Selection With Configurable Kernel Circuits and Adaptive Fusion
item.description: Quantum feature selection (QFS) offers a powerful route to extracting informative features from high-dimensional data by exploiting quantum parallelism and superposition. However, most existing methods focus on single-view data and fail to address the challenges of multiview scenarios, where heterogeneous views must be integrated while maintaining the fidelity of each view. In such scenarios, achieving both interview complementarity and intraview consistency is difficult due to complex dependencies and latent structures within each view. To address this problem, we propose quantum multiview feature selection (QMVFS), a unified framework that combines configurable quantum kernel circuits with adaptive multikernel fusion. For each view, configurable quantum kernel circuits with distinct architectures and parameterizations embed data into a Hilbert space, producing diverse kernel representations. An integrated optimization objective jointly learns view weights, fuses multiple kernels, and enforces sparsity, enabling QMVFS to capture interview synergy while preserving intraview structures. Experiments on six public multiview datasets show that QMVFS outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by an average of 4.44% in classification accuracy, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability for quantum-enhanced multiview learning. Source code is available at: https://github.com/xhchangsha/Quantum-Multi-View-Feature-Selection

item.title: An Arbitrary Register Grouping Scheme for RISC-V Vector Extension: Compilation Support and Hardware Implementation
item.description: Vector instruction set architectures (ISAs) play a critical role in accelerating data-parallel computation, yet mainstream designs—such as the RISC-V “V” vector extension (RVV)—still rely on rigid, power-of-two register grouping strategies. These limitations hinder performance when handling ultralong vectors or nonuniform workloads, as they require extensive strip-mining and careful low-level tuning to maintain efficiency. To overcome these bottlenecks, we propose Zoozve, a flexible, strip-mining-free extension to the RISC-V vector ISA. Zoozve introduces an arbitrary register grouping mechanism that enables more precise register utilization and eliminates the need for data slicing across multiple loop iterations. This work presents a full-stack realization of Zoozve, including 1) a hardware-compatible ISA with support for flexible vector lengths (VLs) and asymmetric instructions; 2) a compiler backend based on LLVM that performs intrinsic splitting, register allocation with live-interval modification, and instruction coalescing; and 3) a hardware proof-of-concept implementation that integrates hazard detection and a register-level element exchange engine. Experimental evaluation using instruction-level simulation shows that Zoozve achieves up to $344.44\times $ speedup in fast Fourier transform (FFT), $76\times $ in dot product, $58.92\times $ in axpy, and $20.41\times $ in 2-D convolution compared to RVV, primarily by eliminating strip-mining and improving register reuse. Register-transfer level (RTL) synthesis in a 40-nm process shows that Zoozve’s additional hardware logic incurs only 9% area overhead, confirming its feasibility for real-world deployment. Together, these results demonstrate Zoozve’s potential as a scalable and efficient vector processing solution for high-performance computing (HPC), machine learning, and signal processing.

item.title: VSTherm: A Virtual Path-Based Stochastic Solver for Full-Chip Leakage-Aware Nonlinear Thermal Simulation
item.description: The continuous advancement of semiconductor processes has led to increasingly prominent leakage power issues in integrated circuits (ICs), making leakage-aware nonlinear thermal simulation a critical challenge in modern chip design. Traditional deterministic field solvers provide high accuracy but suffer from significant computational inefficiencies when handling large-scale mesh structures. Conversely, stochastic methods offer rapid computation speeds but are inherently limited to single-point solutions, preventing them from effectively addressing nonlinear thermal problems. To address this challenge, we propose a virtual path-based stochastic solver that enables efficient leakage-aware thermal simulation. The virtual path algorithm decomposes each real path in Brownian motion into virtual paths, extending stochastic solvers from single-point solutions to regional solutions, allowing a stochastic method to achieve full-chip thermal simulation for the first time, thus enabling the handling of nonlinearity. Additionally, we further accelerate the iteration process by reusing the path trajectories from the first solution process. Extensive experimental evaluations demonstrate that our method achieves a speedup of $20.17\times $ – $52.23\times $ compared to the state-of-the-art solver 3D-ICE on 4 GPUs across various scenarios while maintaining comparable accuracy.

item.title: ASGF4EPD: An Automated Schematic Generation Framework for Electronic Product Design
item.description: As electronic product design complexity (DC) grows exponentially, traditional manual schematic drawing faces significant challenges, including low efficiency, inconsistent specifications, and high error rates, leading to prolonged design cycles, difficult collaboration, and high repair costs. To address these issues, an automatic schematic generation framework for electronic product design is proposed, called ASGF4EPD. First, a pin rule-based schematic design method is applied. This method determines the specific models and connections of the power-using modules through structured requirements modeling and pin-connection rules. It also uses a combination of voltage hierarchy analysis and backtracking search for power supply module selection to complete the schematic design. Second, a quadtree spatial division-based schematic layout method is applied for efficient canvas space management and module placement. Furthermore, the layout is optimized by fragmented space filling, module moving, and boundary alignment operations. The experimental results show that the proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving an average functional completion rate (FCR) of 100%, an electrical rule checking score (ERCS) of 85.04, and a design time (DT) of 2.96 s on tested problems.

item.title: An FPGA-Efficient CNN Accelerator by Integrating Value-Based Sparsity and Bit-Level Sparsity for Weight Compression
item.description: Quantization and sparsity are key techniques for convolutional neural network (CNN) compression and acceleration. Independent exploration of value-based sparsity (VBS) or bit-level sparsity (BLS) in 8-b weights yields limited gains. We analyze weight distributions of VGG16 and ResNet50 after 4-b quantization and find over 80% zero values with strong near-structured sparsity. On VGG16, 98.11% of 16-weight groups contain at least 8 zero values. Based on this analysis, we propose a two-stage sparse compression (TSSC) method that integrates VBS and BLS to efficiently compress weights. In stage 1, we apply postquantization pruning (PQP) to enforce structured sparsity with at least 8 zero values per 16 weights and utilize value-based structured sparsity (VBSS) to compress these 8 zero values per group. In stage 2, among the remaining weights, we apply column-based BLS (CBBLS) to further compress the remaining weights. Finally, a two-stage sparse accelerator, which integrates the TSSC method and corresponding hardware optimization [hardware-efficient activation selection unit (ASU) and bit-serial multiply–accumulate (BSMAC)], is implemented to accelerate the CNN models. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed TSSC method can reduce the weights of VGG16 and ResNet50 to 0.99 and 0.95 b while maintaining an acceptable accuracy drop. When deployed on a field-programmable gate array (FPGA), our accelerator achieves an 8.08 $\times $ weight compression and 7.13 $\times $ performance improvement compared with the 8-b nonsparse VGG16 model. Compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) accelerators, we achieve 1.95 $\times $ –7.97 $\times $ , 2.00 $\times $ –32.8 $\times $ , and 1.13 $\times $ –6.53 $\times $ improvement in LUT efficiency, equivalent LUT efficiency, and energy efficiency, respectively.

item.title: Cyclic Refresh Algorithm for Ensuring 100% Memory Availability in Gain-Cell Embedded DRAM Macros
item.description: Gain-cell embedded DRAM (GC-eDRAM) is a dense, low-power option for embedded memory implementation; however, it suffers from limited data retention time (DRT) and, therefore, requires periodic refresh operations. This limitation restricts its usage to applications that can tolerate temporary memory blockages. In this work, we propose a cyclic refresh algorithm for GC-eDRAM to ensure 100% memory availability for the user under any user access pattern. A hardware controller that integrates the proposed refresh algorithm was developed, synthesized, and evaluated within a System Verilog simulation framework, demonstrating its functionality, silicon area footprint, and power consumption across diverse workloads and access patterns. The area overhead of the proposed algorithm was significantly smaller than that of state-of-the-art solutions, allowing for a reduced silicon footprint even for relatively small macro sizes, achieving as much as a 40% area reduction compared to standard 6-transistor (6T) static random-access memory (SRAM) solutions. By using this algorithm, GC-eDRAM can be a drop-in replacement for SRAM, providing a high-density, low-power embedded memory solution.
